days.title: Placement 1 + how this works
goals: Learn how the app grades handwriting

sections.title: How Week 0 works
sections.explanation:
This week has no new flashcards. Each day is one **placement test** part (about 20 minutes). Your answers save as you go.

- **Kanji parts (1–3):** read the word (type the reading in **kana**), then **handwrite** the kanji. Writing is graded stroke by stroke: shape, direction and order. Tap **Hint** if you're stuck, or **I don't know** to skip.
- **Part 4:** reading only, a sample of N3 and N2 kanji.
- **Part 5:** vocabulary meanings, N4–N2.
- **Part 6:** grammar and dictation.

When you're done, copy the summary (漢字 tab) into the curriculum chat. It sets your kanji lists for Phase A.

You can start before Monday: the placement test is also on the 今日 and 漢字 tabs.

days.title: Placement 2 + pitch accent key
goals: Read the pitch-accent notation used on every card

sections.title: Pitch accent: the notation
sections.explanation:
Japanese words have a **pitch pattern**: each mora is high or low, and the place where pitch **drops** is part of the word. Cards show it as kana with a line over the high morae, a tick where it drops, and a number:

| Number | Name | Shape | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| [0] | heiban (flat) | low → high, no drop (even before a particle) | {端|はし} はし[0] |
| [1] | atamadaka | high on the first mora, then drops | {箸|はし} はし[1] |
| [n] (inside the word) | nakadaka | rises, then drops before the word ends | {卵|たまご} たまご[2] |
| [n] (= number of morae) | odaka | rises, drops only on the following particle | {橋|はし} はし[2] |

Colors on cards: **blue** = heiban, **red** = atamadaka, **orange** = nakadaka, **green** = odaka.

Counting morae: small ゃゅょ join the kana before them (きょ = 1 mora); っ, ん and ー each count as one.
examples: {箸|はし}で{食|た}べる。 (chopsticks, はし[1])
{橋|はし}を{渡|わた}る。 (bridge, はし[2])
{道|みち}の{端|はし}を{歩|ある}く。 (edge, はし[0])

sections.title: {東京|とうきょう}の{思|おも}い{出|で}
sections.text:
{私|わたし}は{前|まえ}に{東京|とうきょう}に{住|す}んでいました。{毎朝|まいあさ}、{電車|でんしゃ}で{日本語|にほんご}の{学校|がっこう}に{通|かよ}っていました。{電車|でんしゃ}はいつも{込|こ}んでいましたが、{窓|まど}から{見|み}える{町|まち}の{景色|けしき}が{好|す}きでした。

{授業|じゅぎょう}の{後|あと}は、{友達|ともだち}とラーメンを{食|た}べに{行|い}ったり、{本屋|ほんや}で{漫画|まんが}を{探|さが}したりしました。{漢字|かんじ}を{覚|おぼ}えるのは{大変|たいへん}でしたが、{少|すこ}しずつ{読|よ}めるようになりました。

{今年|ことし}はもう{一度|いちど}、{漢字|かんじ}を{手|て}で{書|か}いて{覚|おぼ}えるつもりです。
sections.translation:
I used to live in Tokyo. Every morning I commuted by train to a Japanese language school. The trains were always crowded, but I liked the view of the city from the window.

After class I went out for ramen with friends or looked for manga at bookstores. Memorizing kanji was hard, but little by little I became able to read them.

This year I intend to learn kanji again by writing them by hand.

items.prompt: {私|わたし}は{毎朝|まいあさ}{何|なに}で{学校|がっこう}に{通|かよ}っていましたか。
{授業|じゅぎょう}の{後|あと}、{何|なに}をしましたか。
options: ラーメンを{食|た}べに{行|い}ったり、{漫画|まんが}を{探|さが}したりした
{家|いえ}で{漢字|かんじ}を{書|か}いた
{窓|まど}から{町|まち}を{見|み}た

items.prompt: {少|すこ}しずつ{読|よ}める___になりました。
items.explanation: Potential form + ようになる = came to be able to.

items.mnemonic: A man **going** (彳) to the **temple** (寺) has to **wait** in line.
You **hold** the **temple** (寺) offering in your **hand** (扌).
A **cow** (牛) living at a **temple** (寺) is something **special**.

items.audio: {駅|えき}で{友達|ともだち}を{待|ま}っています。
answers: えきでともだちをまっています
items.en: I'm waiting for a friend at the station.

items.prompt: {荷物|にもつ}を___ってあげましょうか。

sections.prompt: In 3–4 sentences, write about a place you lived in Japan. Write it by hand on paper first, then type it here.
sections.modelAnswer: {私|わたし}は{東京|とうきょう}の{中野|なかの}に{住|す}んでいました。{駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くに{安|やす}くておいしい{店|みせ}がたくさんありました。
